findings.title: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a new instance, discarding logged calls on the original `TestLogger`
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. Callers in tests hold a reference to the original `*TestLogger` and inspect `f.InfoLogs`, `f.ErrorLogs`, etc., after exercising code under test. With `LoggerMiddleware` now calling `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, any logs written through `FromContext` are recorded on the newly allocated `TestLogger` and silently lost on the original `TestLogger`, breaking existing `logger_middleware_test.go` assertions (and any other test that inspects `TestLogger` fields after `FromContext` is used). `FromContext` (and likely `New`) should return `f`.

findings.title: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` dereferences `req` without nil checks
findings.body: `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` unconditionally access `req.PluginContext` before passing the call to `m.next`. Other client middlewares in this package (including `LoggerMiddleware` right after it in the chain) explicitly guard against `req == nil` and forward to `m.next` when `req` is nil. Because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` sits ahead of `LoggerMiddleware`, a nil request will now panic with a nil pointer dereference instead of being safely passed through.
